cliff_mechanism_found.observation: Hulk recall collapses from ~100% to 30.85% between tau_A=0.195 and tau_A=0.20 -- far sharper and far earlier than a naive percentile reading of Hulk's raw loss distribution would predict (naive 90%-recall crossing was estimated at ~0.3358).
cliff_mechanism_found.verification: Checked directly: ALL 2000 DoS Hulk window losses under Model A are >= 0.2122 (none below 0.20), so a static threshold at tau_A=0.20 implies 100% recall by raw loss alone -- the real collapse is caused by sr.AdaptiveThresholdController's own warm-up dynamics, not a raw-loss percentile crossing.
cliff_mechanism_found.mechanism: AdaptiveThresholdController seeds its own dynamic threshold BEFORE any window is observed at exactly 1.125 x base_threshold (seed ema_loss=0.75*base, seed ema_std=0.15*base, so seed dynamic_tau = base*(0.75+2.5*0.15) = 1.125*base). At the CURRENT tau_a=0.187660, this seed (0.2112) already sits almost exactly at DoS Hulk's own lowest-loss window (0.2122) -- a razor-thin, already near-zero margin. Any increase to base_threshold raises this seed above the attack block's earliest low-loss windows, which get wrongly assimilated into the adaptive baseline as "normal" (AdaptiveThresholdController only incorporates non-anomalous windows), triggering the same EMA-assimilation runaway batch 11 diagnosed for a different scenario and collapsing recall for the rest of the block.
